subject: Post-call: Acme pricing & token volume follow-up
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Jones <alice.jones@acme.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Acme pricing & token volume follow-up

Hi Alice — great to chat this morning. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery:

Summary of needs:
- Primary use: customer support triage + threaded summarization (multi-turn chat).
- Expected average context window: 1k tokens; peak 4k for long threads.
- Typical request distribution: 70% short answers (~150 tokens generated), 30% long summaries (~800 tokens).
- Target latency: sub-600ms 90th perc for short answers.

Pricing/volume signals you gave on the call:
- Pilot: ~10k interactions/month (est ~2.5M tokens generated/month).
- Q4 growth target: 1–2M interactions/month (est 250M–500M tokens/month).
- Budget band: target $/1M tokens between $60–$120 depending on SLA & feature set.

What I promised to send:
1) A first-pass invoice estimate and unit economics model (attached: acme_pricing_calculator_v2.xlsx).
2) Raw per-interaction token model (.csv) that maps to the calculator (attached: acme_token_model.csv).
3) A one-page invoice estimate PDF for procurement (attached: redwood_invoice_estimate_20270809.pdf).

Key assumptions in the model (high level):
- Model: Open-Chat-Large-v2 (quantized) for cost baseline, with fallback to Open-Chat-Large-v1 for peak capacity.
- Effective generation tokens per interaction (pilot): 300 avg.
- Caching: we assumed 10% prefix reuse for repeat questions.
- Batching: we applied a conservative batching uplift of 15% token efficiency for backend.

Please review the calculator and call out any number that should change (e.g., avg tokens per interaction, expected concurrency). If the budget band is still accurate, I can produce a formal SOW and an updated invoice for procurement.

Next steps:
- Alice: confirm whether the pilot token estimate (2.5M) or the Q4 growth target is the right basis for procurement.
- Redwood: I'll turn this into a formal estimate and propose a procurement timeline + contract language options.

Thanks — attaching the files.

Cheers,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: acme_pricing_calculator_v2.xlsx (Excel spreadsheet, 48 KB)]
[Attachment: acme_token_model.csv (CSV, 8 KB)]
[Attachment: redwood_invoice_estimate_20270809.pdf (PDF, 12 KB)]

From: Alice Jones <alice.jones@acme.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Aug 2027 09:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call: Acme pricing & token volume follow-up

Thanks, Sean — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Token volumes: the 1–2M interactions/month was a top-of-funnel projection for product marketing later in Q4. For procurement and pilot sizing, please base the initial estimate on 25k interactions/month (pilot) -> ~7.5M tokens/month. We expect pilot to run for 3 months.

2) Budget: the $60–$120/1M tokens band is in the right neighborhood. Procurement asked if we can target <= $75/1M tokens for the pilot to keep the POC within their initial budget. If we can show a path to $50–$60/1M at scale (post-qtr), that'd be ideal.

3) Discounts: any standard pilot credits or consumption-based sliding discounts you can offer? Also, do you have an SLA-backed option that hits the 600ms 90th percentile target?

Tom will own procurement on our side; loop him in for contract items. We'll review the spreadsheet and get back with any adjustments by EOD Friday.

Alice
Director, Product — Acme Corp

Thanks Alice — appreciate the clarifications. Updated notes and asks below, plus an adjusted invoice estimate attached.

What I changed in the model:
- Pilot baseline: 25k interactions/month -> 7.5M tokens/month (avg 300 tokens/generated).
- Pilot duration modeled: 3 months.
- Unit economics: baseline unit price $85/1M tokens (reflects pilot discount) -> pilot monthly cost ~ $637.50 for generation tokens.
- Platform/service add-ons: monitoring & retention (30 days) + private VPC option shown as line items in the spreadsheet.
- SLA option: we included an SLA-backed pricing row that adds a latency premium (approx +22% on token rate) to meet 600ms 90th for the short-answer profile.

Quick math (pilot):
- Tokens/month (pilot): 7,500,000 tokens
- Unit price (pilot discounted): $85 / 1M -> monthly token cost = 7.5 * $85 = $637.50
- Estimated infra and fixed fees (per-month): $1,200 (dedicated warm pool reservation for predictable latency)
- Total monthly (pilot): ~$1,837.50 -> 3-month pilot total ~$5,512.50

Path to scale:
- At 250M tokens/month we show unit price falling to ~$55/1M tokens (volume + committed capacity discounts + quantization options).

Attachments included in this email:
- acme_pricing_calculator_v2.xlsx (updated with pilot row and SLA option)
- acme_token_model.csv (updated token distribution assumptions)
- redwood_invoice_estimate_20270809.pdf (one-page procurement-ready estimate)

Next steps I propose:
1) Sean/Redwood: provide an updated formal quote and SOW by EOD Tuesday including: pilot start date options, payment terms, and standard pilot credit we can apply.
2) Acme: confirm whether procurement wants the invoice at the pilot baseline (7.5M tokens/mo) or the larger Q4 projection for negotiations.
3) Schedule a 30-min procurement sync (Monica to propose windows).

If <= $75/1M is a hard requirement for the pilot, we can explore an introductory pilot credit to bridge to $75/1M effective rate — I noted that as an internal approval ask.

Happy to jump on a quick call if that helps.

Regards,
Sean
